# Classification of Fusion Categories with Three Simple Object Types

In this work, we classify all fusion categories corresponding to a given set of fusion rules with three simple object types. Fusion categories are algebraic structures that generalize the representation theory of finite groups and quantum groups, and their classification is a central problem in the field. By fixing the fusion rules—the combinatorial data specifying how tensor products of simple objects decompose—we determine every possible categorical structure compatible with these rules in the case of three simple object types.

Our results have significant implications for the broader classification program. Specifically, if a conjecture of Ostrik holds true, our work completes the full classification of fusion categories with three simple object types. This would resolve an important open case and provide a comprehensive understanding of these categories, contingent only on the validity of Ostrik's conjecture.

A central methodological contribution of this paper is the introduction of a convenient, concrete, and useful variation of graphical calculus for fusion categories. Graphical calculus provides an intuitive diagrammatic language for reasoning about morphisms and their compositions, and our variant is designed to be both accessible and computationally effective. This framework streamlines calculations that would otherwise be cumbersome in purely algebraic terms.

We employ this graphical framework to discuss the fundamental concepts of pivotality and sphericity. These structural properties, which concern the existence and behavior of duality data within a fusion category, play a crucial role in the theory. Our approach clarifies these notions and makes them more transparent through the lens of the diagrammatic calculus.

Finally, as an application of our methods, we provide a short and elementary re-proof that the quadruple dual functor is naturally isomorphic to the identity. This result, originally established by more involved techniques, follows readily within our framework, demonstrating the practical utility of the graphical calculus we have developed.

# Classification of Fusion Categories with Three Simple Object Types

## Introduction

Fusion categories are semisimple tensor categories with finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects, a unit object that is simple, and rigid duals for every object. They arise naturally in a variety of contexts, including quantum field theory, the theory of subfactors, quantum groups, and topological phases of matter. A central problem in the field is the classification of fusion categories that realize a given set of fusion rules—that is, a given decomposition of tensor products of simple objects into direct sums of simple objects. This combinatorial data constrains, but does not fully determine, the categorical structure, and the task of enumerating all categorifications of a fixed fusion ring remains difficult in general.

## The Main Result

In this work, the researchers undertake the classification of all fusion categories associated with a particular set of fusion rules involving three types of simple objects. Fusion categories with a small number of simple objects have been the subject of sustained study, since they provide tractable yet nontrivial testing grounds for structural conjectures. The case of three simple object types occupies an important intermediate position: it is rich enough to exhibit subtle phenomena while still being amenable to explicit analysis.

To carry out the classification, the authors develop and employ a variation of the standard graphical calculus for tensor categories. Graphical, or diagrammatic, calculus encodes morphisms as string diagrams, allowing algebraic identities to be manipulated pictorially. The refinement introduced here is specifically designed to handle the subtleties of **pivotality** and **sphericity**. A pivotal structure is a monoidal natural isomorphism between the identity functor and the double dual functor, and a spherical structure imposes a compatibility condition ensuring that left and right traces agree. These structures are essential for defining consistent quantum dimensions and for relating fusion categories to invariants of knots, links, and three-manifolds. By carefully tracking how the graphical relations interact with pivotal and spherical data, the authors are able to constrain the possible fusion categories and enumerate them completely.

## Dependence on an Ostrik Conjecture

The classification is not unconditional: it depends on the validity of a conjecture due to Ostrik. Ostrik's conjectures concern the structure and realizability of fusion categories with restricted fusion data, and they encode expectations about which combinatorial fusion rings can be categorified and in how many ways. Contingent upon the truth of the relevant Ostrik conjecture, the present results fill in the remaining case needed to complete the full classification of fusion categories with three simple object types. In this sense, the paper closes a chapter in an ongoing program: together with previously known cases, the new classification exhausts all possibilities for fusion categories built from three simple objects.

## A New Proof of Radford-Type Behavior

Beyond the classification itself, the methods yield an independent dividend. A celebrated result in the theory of tensor categories—related to Radford's formula for the fourth power of the antipode in Hopf algebras—asserts that the **quadruple dual functor** is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor. The quadruple dual arises from applying the duality operation four times; while the single and double duals may differ substantially from the identity, the fourth iterate is remarkably tame. In the categorical setting, the statement that the quadruple dual is naturally isomorphic to the identity is a deep structural fact, ordinarily established using sophisticated machinery.

The graphical techniques introduced for the classification provide an **elementary re-proof** of this fact in the setting under consideration. Because the refined calculus makes the interaction between duality and pivotal structure transparent, the natural isomorphism between the quadruple dual and the identity emerges directly from diagrammatic reasoning, without recourse to the heavier apparatus typically invoked. This re-proof both illuminates the underlying mechanism and demonstrates the broader utility of the pivotality- and sphericity-sensitive graphical calculus.

## Conclusion

Taken together, these results advance the classification program for small fusion categories and refine the diagrammatic tools available for their study. The completion of the three-simple-object case—modulo the Ostrik conjecture—provides a clearer map of the landscape of fusion categories, while the elementary re-derivation of the quadruple dual isomorphism showcases how careful attention to pivotal and spherical structure can yield conceptual as well as computational rewards.

# Victor Ostrik and His Contributions to Mathematics

Victor Ostrik is a distinguished mathematician whose work has significantly influenced the fields of representation theory, tensor categories, and modern algebra. Currently a professor at the University of Oregon, Ostrik has earned international recognition for his deep contributions to the study of algebraic structures.

## Research Focus

Ostrik's research primarily centers on **tensor categories** and **fusion categories**, which are mathematical frameworks that generalize the notion of representations of groups. These structures have profound connections to a wide range of areas, including quantum groups, conformal field theory, and mathematical physics. His work helps mathematicians and physicists understand symmetry in abstract algebraic settings.

One of the notable aspects of his research involves the classification and analysis of **module categories** over fusion categories. This area explores how abstract categorical objects can act on one another, revealing hidden symmetries and structural relationships that are essential for both pure mathematics and applications in theoretical physics.

## Collaborative Work

Ostrik is well known for his collaborations, particularly with mathematicians such as Pavel Etingof and Dmitri Nikshych. Together, they have produced influential works, including foundational texts on tensor categories that serve as important references for researchers entering the field. Their collaborative textbook on tensor categories is widely regarded as a standard resource for graduate students and specialists alike.

## Impact and Legacy

The significance of Ostrik's work lies in its ability to bridge seemingly disparate areas of mathematics. His results have provided tools that are used in the study of quantum symmetries, topological quantum computing, and the mathematical foundations of modern physics. By developing rigorous frameworks and proving key theorems, he has helped shape the direction of contemporary research in categorical algebra.

## Conclusion

Victor Ostrik exemplifies the modern mathematician whose work combines abstraction with wide-reaching applications. Through his research, teaching, and collaborations, he continues to advance our understanding of the deep algebraic structures that underlie much of modern mathematics and theoretical physics.

**Abstract**

A fusion category is a semisimple $\mathbb{C}$-linear rigid monoidal category with finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects and simple unit object. In this paper we undertake a complete classification of fusion categories of rank three, i.e., those possessing exactly three isomorphism classes of simple objects. Building on the structure of the associated fusion rings and the constraints imposed by the pentagon and hexagon (where applicable) equations, we first enumerate all possible based rings of rank three that are categorifiable, distinguishing those admitting a nontrivial grading, those arising as near-group fusion rings, and those with a self-dual or non-self-dual simple object structure. We show that every such fusion category falls into one of a small number of families: those Morita equivalent to pointed categories associated to abelian groups of order dividing $9$, the near-group categories of type $\mathbb{Z}/3 + \mathbb{Z}/3$ and their relatives, and the categories arising from quantum groups at roots of unity, notably the even part of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_4$ and $\mathrm{SU}(3)$-type constructions. Using techniques from Galois symmetry of modular data, Frobenius–Perron dimensions, and the theory of module categories, we determine precisely which fusion rings admit categorifications and count the inequivalent categorical structures on each, resolving the question of uniqueness up to monoidal equivalence. As an application, we describe the braided and modular structures supported by these categories and their Drinfeld centers, and we highlight several rigidity phenomena that obstruct categorification. Our results extend the known classifications in ranks one and two and provide a foundation for the study of higher-rank fusion categories.

counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.** We give a complete classification of pivotal fusion categories admitting a compatible family of dualizing structures over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, resolving a conjecture of the second author in the finite-rank case. Our main theorem asserts that every such category is equivalent, as a rigid monoidal category, to a category of representations of a canonically associated weak Hopf algebroid, and that the equivalence is unique up to a torsor over the group of monoidal natural automorphisms of the identity functor. As a corollary we obtain a bijection between equivalence classes of these categories and a set of combinatorial data consisting of a based root datum together with a cohomological obstruction class lying in a suitably defined third Hochschild group.

The proof rests on three technical contributions of independent interest. First, we develop a graphical calculus for morphisms in pivotal categories in which duality is realized by planar isotopy, and we prove a coherence theorem showing that any two diagrammatic evaluations of a closed labeled graph agree; this reduces the verification of the key coassociativity constraints to a finite set of local moves. Second, we introduce the notion of a *dual functor* between such categories—a monoidal functor intertwining the left and right dualization structures up to a specified 2-cocycle—and establish that the 2-category of pivotal categories, dual functors, and monoidal transformations is biequivalent to a strictification whose 1-morphisms admit a normal form. Third, using this normal form we prove a rigidity result: any dual functor inducing an isomorphism on Grothendieck rings and preserving the pivotal trace is automatically an equivalence.

Along the way we compute the relevant obstruction groups for several infinite families, verify that all realizable data occur, and exhibit explicit generators and relations for the graphical presentation. We conclude with applications to the reconstruction of modular tensor categories from their fusion subcategories and remark on the failure of the classification in positive characteristic, where new phenomena governed by the Frobenius twist appear.
